title: Quiz: Market Basket Analysis and Apriori

questions.text: The rule {bread, butter} → {milk} has support = 0.12. This means:
options: 12% of transactions contain bread, butter, and milk together
12% of transactions that contain bread and butter also contain milk
Milk appears in 12% of all transactions
The rule is correct 12% of the time
questions.explanation: Support is the fraction of all transactions containing the complete itemset (bread ∩ butter ∩ milk). It is NOT the conditional probability — that is confidence.

options: The antecedent and consequent are statistically independent
The rule occurs in fewer transactions than expected
The rule should be discarded because it is incorrect
questions.explanation: Lift = confidence / support(consequent). If lift = 1, the confidence equals the unconditional probability of the consequent — meaning knowing the antecedent provides no additional information. The items are independent.

questions.text: The Apriori principle states: if an itemset is frequent, all of its subsets are also frequent.
questions.explanation: This is the anti-monotone property. If {bread, butter, milk} is frequent (above minSupport), then {bread, butter}, {bread, milk}, and {butter, milk} must also be frequent. Apriori uses the contrapositive: if a subset is infrequent, its supersets cannot be frequent.

questions.text: What does the `transactions` class in the arules package store internally?
options: A data frame with one row per item purchased
A sparse binary matrix of transaction × item presence/absence
A list of character vectors, one per transaction
questions.explanation: The transactions class is a sparse binary matrix where rows are transactions and columns are items. A 1 indicates the item was present in that transaction. Sparse representation is efficient because most entries are 0 (an item not purchased).

questions.text: Setting minSupport very low (e.g. 0.0001) in Apriori will:
options: Produce fewer rules with higher confidence
Eliminate the need to check lift
Produce an exponentially large number of candidate itemsets, making computation slow
Make the algorithm run faster by pruning more branches
questions.explanation: The Apriori pruning relies on infrequent itemsets having infrequent supersets. With a very low minSupport threshold, almost all itemsets are 'frequent', so almost no pruning occurs, and the number of candidate itemsets grows exponentially.
